title: Rouzleweave #2 (May 2002)
author: Perry Kinman (editor)
card_summary: Rouzleweave #2 (May 2002), a PKD fanzine edited by Perry Kinman, 37 pages, JIS B5 format. Digitized in March 2017 by Frank Hollander from a photocopy of the original print run, with Kinman supplying scans of pages 36–37 where Hollander's photocopies were defective. Part of the early-2000s wave of PKD fan-press publishing alongside PKDS Newsletter and the early issues of PKD Otaku.
page_summary:
Rouzleweave #2 (May 2002) is a PKD fanzine edited by Perry Kinman, distributed in print at JIS B5 format (182 × 257 mm) in a small run. The 37-page issue is part of the early-2000s wave of PKD fan-press publishing that ran alongside the long-established PKDS Newsletter (Paul Williams's vehicle for the Estate-aligned fan readership) and the then-emergent PKD Otaku (Patrick Clark and Frank Hollander). The fanzine's distribution was small enough that Frank Hollander, working in March 2017 to digitize and preserve the issue, had to obtain it indirectly and was missing complete pages 36–37 from his own photocopy — Kinman supplied replacement scans for those pages.

Fan-press position: Rouzleweave belongs to the same lineage as Bruce Gillespie's Australian SF Commentary (which had published PKD-focused issues in the 1970s) and as the post-1982 PKDS Newsletter — small-run amateur publishing where serious PKD scholarship and reader-discussion intersect, often containing material (correspondence excerpts, fan-research findings, contemporary memoir) not available in academic venues. The Hollander digitization (March 2017) is the standard preservation copy, distributed informally among PKD fan-academics with Hollander's note 'Feel free to use these files as you wish. I can only assume Perry would have wanted any interested Philip K. Dick fans to have access to this wonderful fanzine.'

Documentary value: (1) preservation of an otherwise hard-to-find early-2000s PKD fanzine; (2) part of the institutional history of PKD fan publishing that bridges the print-zine era (PKDS Newsletter, SF Commentary) and the web era (Total Dick-Head, post-2007); (3) one of multiple small-run fan publications that have operated as venues for PKD scholarship outside the academic mainstream; (4) Frank Hollander's preservation work itself is an example of the field's fan-academic curatorship in the lineage of his PKD Otaku editorship.

Format note: the source files are scanned JPEG images of the original print pages (numbered 2-01 through 2-37), distributed via a 2017 zip archive bundled with Hollander's README. No OCR-extracted text is currently available; the issue's contents will require manual or OCR-assisted summarization for inclusion in the term and segment cross-link graph.
